note: Mutation testing answers what coverage cannot: whether an assertion
catches a wrong value or merely executes the line. This file is a
ratchet, not a target -- survivors must not grow.
Not every survivor is a gap. Roughly a quarter change a log or error
message, which nothing asserts on by design. Others are equivalent:
the guard `if not mismatched` only decides when the read-back loop
exits, not what it returns, so killing it would require asserting on
timing -- a worse test than the mutant is a risk.
'not_covered' is code the in-process tests never execute: the CLI,
session and process modules are driven through a real subprocess,
which loads the checked-out source rather than the mutant. See
